questions.explain: Granular cost reporting (team/application/feature level) consistently identifies 20–35% in previously invisible waste within 90 days. The mechanism: when a team sees their recommendation engine's nightly batch costs $4,200/month while the feature drives <$800/month in revenue, the optimization conversation practically has itself.
options: Granular reporting identifies 20–35% invisible waste in 90 days — e.g., a $4,200/mo batch job driving <$800/mo revenue makes optimization obvious
questions.q: What value does per-team/per-app/per-feature cost reporting deliver?

questions.explain: The workable minimum taxonomy is five tags: team, app, environment, feature, cost-center — starting with too many tags and enforcing none leaves 40% untagged and discredits the reports. Keep feature optional for initial rollout (forcing it prematurely creates inconsistent data), and enforce tags at resource creation (SCP/Azure Policy/org policy) — otherwise untagged resources accumulate in an unattributed bucket.
options: Five tags minimum: team, app, environment, feature, cost-center (feature optional initially); enforce at creation or untagged resources pile up in an unattributed bucket
questions.q: What tagging taxonomy supports cost attribution, and why enforce at creation?

questions.explain: Prefix every query at the application layer with a structured comment: /* app:checkout-service team:payments feature:cart-totals */ — Query Store/sys.dm_exec_sql_text capture the full query text including comments, so the comment is parsed out with PATINDEX/STRING_SPLIT. Cost proxy = total_worker_time + (total_logical_reads × 8.0), apportioned against the instance's actual monthly cost.
options: Embed /* app:X team:Y feature:Z */ comments in queries at the application layer; parse them from Query Store text and attribute with cost_proxy = worker_time + logical_reads×8.0
Comments are stripped by Query Store
questions.q: How do you attribute database cost to specific features and queries?

questions.explain: A finops star schema: dim_teams, dim_apps, dim_features, dim_db_instances feeding fact_infra_costs (from cloud billing APIs — tells what a team spent) and fact_query_costs (from Query Store snapshots — tells which features drove it). That join is the complete picture: team spend + responsible features/queries.
options: finops star schema: dim_teams/apps/features/db_instances with fact_infra_costs (billing APIs → what was spent) + fact_query_costs (Query Store → which features drove it)
questions.q: What reporting schema unifies infrastructure and query-level cost data?

questions.explain: Handle the untagged backlog with a quarterly tagging sprint: pull all untagged resources, assign to account owners by VPC/subnet, require tagging within 30 days or charge back to a shared pool — the shared-pool penalty is the behavioral incentive. Then automate weekly digest emails to engineering leads so no one must run manual exports.
options: Quarterly tagging sprint with 30-day deadline and shared-pool chargeback penalty, plus automated weekly digest emails to engineering leads
questions.q: How do you handle the untagged backlog and keep reporting automatic?
